metadata.scope: Public rustia project readiness, based on the current workspace and canonical design docs.
notes: Percentages are rough engineering estimates, not automated metrics.
The scope tracks public rustia crates, conformance, benchmarks, docs, tooling, and release readiness.
Project pillars and non-goals are canonical in design/02-pillars.md.
The public host-bridge remains generic; grabby-specific types and effect catalogs stay outside public rustia.

benchmark_adapters.note: mlua-lua54 runs separately from mlua-luau because both mlua-sys builds use links = "lua"; mlua-luau-jit is an explicit execution mode in the mlua-luau adapter family.

memory_safety.failure: catchable atomic OutOfMemory after one forced collection
memory_safety.telemetry: live, reserved, and optional instruction-boundary peak bytes

decision_reset.preserves: VM configuration, host services, extensions, installed host functions/modules, lifetime memory peaks, and host-owned immutable compiled modules
decision_reset.discards: guest globals, heap objects, coroutines, loaded programs, caches, coverage, tracebacks, and retained roots
decision_reset.restarts: RNG, logical time, instruction counters, compatibility GC state, and deterministic collection scheduling
decision_reset.retained_handle_rule: all Function, Exports, and RetainedValue leases are epoch-checked and stale after reset

typed_invocation.schema: lifetime-independent HostSchema plus a freshly borrowed HostContext per invocation
typed_invocation.authority: sealed Input, Slots, Effects, and SlotWrites views; profile-gated HostMut access
typed_invocation.budgets: one shared fuel budget plus bounded record count and logical record bytes
typed_invocation.commit: per-host-call savepoints and outer publication after guest execution, snapshotting, and typed conversion
typed_invocation.hard_abort: fuel, OOM, record overflow, yield-boundary violations, missing dispatch, and host panic
typed_invocation.panic_recovery: contain host functions, typed dispatch, extension ops, stdout/clocks, and loadstring compiler; discard records and poison the VM until decision reset
typed_invocation.rollback_scope: staged records only, not guest heap/global state, HostMut mutation, or host interior mutability

wasm_target_bench.note: The recurring wasm target runner executes rustia, koto, and rhai on Node/V8; the earlier four-runtime matrix is retained as historical portability evidence.

wasm_dispatch_bench.note: The recurring dispatch check runs on Node/V8; historical cross-engine evidence also found call_ref slower than br_table.

overall_goals.name: Whole public rustia project
overall_goals.state: The architecture is locked and production crates are substantial: the safe-Rust VM/compiler, pending-free pinned conformance corpus, host-pluggable output/time services, host-owned canonical-identity require resolution/cache, lifetime-safe per-invocation host contexts, bounded transactional effect journals, CLI, benchmark matrix, private HotIR, closure-call PIC, generation-safe object/program reclamation, VM-owned memory telemetry, logical-live quotas, atomic catchable OOM, epoch-safe decision reset, and exact dedicated-Linux native plus wasm quota evidence are in-tree. The remaining release gates are O(1) quota accounting, broader mixed-heap pressure evidence, rich/live values, semantic-tail hardening, and packaging.
overall_goals.future_plan: Finish O(1) accounting and broader mixed-heap pressure evidence; complete the rich-value boundary and transactional failure semantics; then continue measured optimization and public release work.

overall_goals.name: Usable embedded scripting crate
overall_goals.state: The facade now includes typed run/compile, owned scalar/table conversions, host-owned canonical-identity require resolution/cache, a lifetime-independent HostSchema with fresh borrowed HostContext values per invocation, capability-specific host views, shared fuel, bounded transactional record publication, usage receipts, retained functions/exports with true collector roots plus install-generation and decision-epoch checks, owned-value serde, extensions, hot reload, epoch-safe decision reset, examples, diagnostics, migration guidance, host-pluggable stdout/clock services, VM-owned memory telemetry, and configurable logical-live quotas. It is not yet a complete rich embedding boundary: graph-preserving rich values, a live zero-copy serde path, transactional guest-side failure rollback, and an O(1) quota counter remain.
overall_goals.future_plan: Complete O(1) accounting, rich/live values, transactional failure semantics, diagnostics, and API stabilization.

overall_goals.name: Full public standalone Luau engine release
overall_goals.state: The Luau 0.709 standalone target and 493-ref conformance denominator are strong. Bounded generation-safe object/program lifetimes, VM-owned live/reserved/peak telemetry, logical-live memory limits, atomic catchable OOM, host-owned require resolution/cache, lifetime-safe typed invocations with transactional records, and versioned deterministic reset/module lifecycles are implemented; native Linode plus wasm quota evidence is exact. Release still requires O(1) quota accounting, broader mixed-heap pressure evidence, richer value interop, transactional guest-module failure semantics, semantic-tail/diagnostic hardening, the full correctness/golden target matrix, and packaging. Analyzer/typechecker, raw C API, Roblox, Lua 5.4, and bytecode compatibility are not runtime-release requirements.
overall_goals.future_plan: Close the remaining accounting and host-boundary gates, harden the semantic tail and cross-target goldens, then package and publish against the pinned target.

overall_goals.name: Standalone benchmark OSS project
overall_goals.state: Harness, package metadata, split notes, machine-readable inventory, current-results JSON, generated claim gate, history, a standalone target-first current-results HTML report with interpreter-only and best-mode rankings plus cold-start costs, five default workload families, 18 workload entries with cross-adapter #15 string-building source coverage and six synthetic/realistic memory probes, all 12 requested adapters plus a verified mlua/Luau JIT mode, exact ephemeral-Linux fixed-throughput and evidence-only memory protocols, a recurring wasm target runner for rustia+koto+rhai on Node/V8, retained cross-engine wasm evidence, a call_ref versus br_table dispatch microbench, and an explicit dedicated-Linode native-plus-wasm matrix lifecycle are present.
overall_goals.future_plan: Split from the workspace, add the interop/serde/fuel-limit tranche and regression alerts, and accumulate longer-run public history.

overall_goals.name: Public release readiness
overall_goals.state: License, generated crate metadata audit, explicit internal dependency versions, release-preflight-enforced examples, migration guidance, CLI/diagnostics, typed owned values and callbacks, true-root epoch-safe retained handles, host signature/fuel metadata, output/time services, VM memory telemetry, logical-live limits with atomic OOM, versioned decision reset, release-readiness and semver policy, hosted CI, benchmark claim gating, package dry-runs, and publishability auditing are present; crates are still workspace-private and release polish is incomplete.
overall_goals.future_plan: Close O(1) accounting, module, value-interop, transactional-install, and semantic-tail gates before removing publish blockers in topological order.

entries.name: Harness and coverage notes

entries.name: Lexer
entries.state: Production lexer crate exists with tests.
entries.future_plan: Expand edge-case coverage as conformance finds parser/lexer gaps.

entries.name: Parser
entries.state: Hand-written parser handles Luau syntax and type-grammar erasure.
entries.future_plan: Continue differential and conformance-driven hardening.

entries.name: Type grammar parse-and-erase
entries.state: Type syntax is parsed for runtime erasure; no typechecker is intended for P1.
entries.future_plan: Defer gradual typechecker/LSP work to public-parity phase.

entries.name: Compiler
entries.state: The production compiler emits bytecode for the pinned corpus and discovers captured bindings before final lowering, enabling direct immutable captures while preserving mutable loop/backedge semantics.
entries.future_plan: Add differential/fuzz coverage for parser/compiler and runtime-error-phase parity, then harden diagnostics, O2 passes, superinstructions, and optimization boundaries.

entries.name: Bytecode dispatch core
entries.state: The portable big-match/br-table interpreter is authoritative. Bounded private HotIR numeric tracelets preserve logical fuel, deterministic-GC policy, and atomic fallback; a four-lane prototype-polymorphic call-site PIC plus direct immutable captures now accelerates the tracked closure workload.
entries.future_plan: Extend verified HotIR effect/control-flow coverage, add profile-led superinstructions/O2 and hot/cold split, and keep fuel, GC, coverage, and fallback semantics invariant.

entries.name: Value representation
entries.state: The sealed 16-byte tagged value, 13-byte inline binary strings, and shared compiled-string references are implemented, documented, and validated by an exact 512-VM Linux sampler.
entries.future_plan: Keep the representation sealed while expanding measurement to realistic mixed heaps and continuing GC work.

entries.name: Heap and GC
entries.state: Standard uses paced gc-arena debt collection, DeterministicSim uses instruction-count full cycles, weak tables are swept, and tables/functions/upvalues/runtime strings/userdata/buffers/vectors plus loaded programs use generation-safe reusable slots. Retained host values are true roots; explicit quiescence reclaims obsolete programs/coroutines and releases spare backing capacity. Reset ABI v1 reuses allocation containers while discarding the complete guest heap and loaded-program state at an idle decision boundary. Exact VM-owned live/reserved accounting, optional peaks, logical-live quotas, forced-collection retry, and atomic catchable OOM are implemented. Cohort safe-memory-588b541 supplies 99 native Linode samples and a wasm32 512 KiB quota/recovery pass.
entries.future_plan: Add O(1) incremental accounting and script counters, broaden mixed-heap pressure coverage, then tune collection intervals.

entries.name: Tables/metatables
entries.state: Broad table, metatable, iteration, and stdlib behavior is conformance-covered. Logical deletion preserves tombstone insertion semantics, larger hash parts use a deterministic side index, and shape-revalidated positive string-slot caches cover global/index reads and writes plus dedicated GETTABLEKS, SETTABLEKS, and NAMECALL field/method paths. Exact OOP candidate ns/unit is 65.959% lower under its accepted Linux protocol; that comparison also includes the weak-table GC-scan correction.
entries.future_plan: Keep the full suite and exact protocol green, then add cached-length refinements and broader adaptive specialization.

entries.name: Functions/coroutines/pcall
entries.state: Functions, closures, varargs, coroutines, and protected calls have broad coverage.
entries.future_plan: Keep stackless recursion and yield paths covered as runtime changes.

entries.name: Base/math/string/bit32/vector/utf8 stdlib
entries.state: Major pinned Luau stdlib surfaces, including buffer, vector, utf8, and string pack/unpack behavior, are fixture-covered. Host-environment output/time services are now provider-backed: print composes tostring/__tostring into a host stdout sink (no-op without one), no-arg os.time/os.date read a wall-clock provider with a pinned-epoch fallback, and os.clock reads a monotonic provider with a deterministic logical-clock fallback. collectgarbage('count') remains zero and gcinfo memory reporting synthetic.
entries.future_plan: Keep the language-library corpus green while replacing compatibility memory counters with the future O(1) quota tracker without exposing nondeterministic process RSS.

entries.name: Error/debug behavior
entries.state: Debug/error behavior is substantially covered for conformance, and public rustia errors expose source-span/runtime-location accessors for diagnostic renderers.
entries.future_plan: Tighten VM stack traces and source diagnostics, and prove valid runtime failures remain catchable at runtime rather than moving into compile-time rejection.

entries.name: f64/libm/canonicalization discipline
entries.state: Deterministic number policy is documented and partly enforced by tests.
entries.future_plan: Keep compiler and VM on the same libm/canonicalization rules.

entries.name: Runtime profiles
entries.state: LuauCompat, ReproducibleStandard, and DeterministicSim are concrete runtime profiles. LuauCompat selects Luau-style hash iteration; DeterministicSim omits collectgarbage/gcinfo and optional loadstring, registers the os table iff a deterministic clock provider is plugged, admits a stdout sink on any profile, rejects nondeterministic clock providers, deterministically sweeps weak tables, and rejects external-state/nondeterministic host registrations. Typed invocations make fuel, OOM, record overflow, yield-boundary violations, missing dispatch, and host callback panic hard aborts without changing legacy catchable-OOM behavior. Reset ABI v1 defines a replay-stable idle boundary: host configuration survives, guest state is discarded, deterministic counters restart, and retained handles are epoch-invalidated.
entries.future_plan: Keep the replay and host-fuel ABIs versioned and cross-target tested while O(1) accounting lands.

entries.name: Fuel and limits
entries.state: Instruction fuel exists; legacy roots receive their configured per-execution budget, while a typed invocation shares the lower of its explicit InvocationLimits fuel and the builder/settings ceiling across every guest call. Public host-function fuel metadata carries an ABI version. Reset ABI v1 restarts logical execution and deterministic GC counters. VmSettings::memory_limit_bytes and RustiaBuilder::memory_limit_bytes cap VM-owned logical live bytes with identical native/wasm semantics; pressure forces one collection before a catchable OutOfMemory, and large table/string/buffer requests plus growing table writes are rejected atomically.
entries.future_plan: Replace the correctness-first boundary census with O(1) incremental quota accounting and keep optimized instruction costs replay-stable.

entries.name: Cross-engine wasm proof
entries.state: Production rustia wasm and call_ref vs br_table dispatch are measured across V8, JavaScriptCore-family, and SpiderMonkey; the pre-lock wasm gate is closed.
entries.future_plan: Keep the measurements fresh as the wasm artifact and runtimes evolve.

entries.name: Full target correctness and golden matrix
entries.state: Linux x86_64, macOS arm64, and wasm/V8 golden evidence exists, with retained JavaScriptCore-family and SpiderMonkey shell portability measurements. Hosted CI cross-compiles the portable engine library for the full declared native triple set plus wasm32. Real Intel Mac, Windows, Linux arm64, mobile-native, Firefox, and Safari execution/goldens are not all continuously covered.
entries.future_plan: Execute reproducible cross-target goldens on real hosts and browsers for the full design/00-constraints.md matrix without mixing non-dedicated macOS/Windows timings into benchmark history.

entries.name: Koto-shaped facade
entries.state: Builder, typed run<T>, source-named compile/run helpers, public error diagnostic accessors, globals, exports, retained functions, host-owned require resolution/cache, a typed HostSchema/HostContext invocation surface, bounded record transactions, usage receipts, an epoch-safe decision reset, environment presets (standard/deterministic/live) with stdout and determinism-labeled service sockets, examples, and a first koto-to-rustia migration guide exist.
entries.future_plan: Stabilize names and error types, add the rich/live-value layer, and expand migration guidance as the remaining production gates land.

entries.name: Owned value firewall
entries.state: OwnedValue supports nil, booleans, numbers, UTF-8 strings, tree-shaped tables, scalar/Option/Vec/BTreeMap conversions, and typed table helpers. It does not faithfully represent binary strings, buffers, vectors, opaque userdata identity, non-scalar/identity keys, shared/cyclic table graphs, or live VM values.
entries.future_plan: Add bytes/buffers/vectors, opaque identity-safe userdata handles, richer keys, and graph-preserving shared/cyclic tables while keeping internal GC lifetimes behind the facade; full UserData/Scope registration remains optional later work.

entries.name: Typed host functions
entries.state: Plain Rust functions can be registered with typed args/results through arity 8. Typed VMs add sealed Input, Slots, Effects, SlotWrites, and profile-gated HostMut views; namespaced HostModule metadata; explicit fuel; fallible rustia::Result<T> returns; panic containment; parameter-count/type/fallibility metadata; and conversion errors that name the host function plus argument or return position.
entries.future_plan: Keep tightening diagnostics and decide whether public signature metadata should grow beyond Rust type names.

entries.name: Extension/linker layer
entries.state: Namespaced extensions, coarse capabilities, pre-install function metadata including host-fuel ABI version, Rust parameter/return type names, fallibility, deterministic registration validation, and explicit external-state helpers exist.
entries.future_plan: Add migration docs and decide how much internal fuel schedule data should become public.

entries.name: Public host-bridge seam
entries.state: A lifetime-independent HostSchema and freshly borrowed HostContext provide the generic worker-local boundary without public grabby types, boxed/stored context, locks, Any, raw pointers, Send, or a static context. Sealed capability views expose frozen input/slots or a private bounded effect journal; one invocation shares fuel across guest calls; successful records receive dense sequence numbers; per-handler savepoints and an outer transaction cover execution, snapshotting, and conversion; hard resource failures abort; panics from every VM-controlled host callout roll back records and poison the VM until reset. Injectable output/time providers, VM memory telemetry, logical-live limits, and decision reset are also implemented.
entries.future_plan: Prove the complete boundary under long-running host integration and keep the callback-capture/interior-mutability trust boundary explicit.

entries.name: Module loading and resolution
entries.state: CompiledModule install/hot reload and script-visible require are implemented. ServiceModuleResolver keeps resolution in host policy with no ambient filesystem; the host supplies canonical identity and source; successful zero-or-one-result modules execute once per decision epoch; cached values are roots; nested referrers, cycles, shared fuel, reset, deterministic labels, panic poisoning, quota admission, and MODULE_RESOLUTION_ABI_VERSION are covered.
entries.future_plan: Define transactional or isolated rollback for arbitrary guest global/heap side effects from runtime-failing module installation and hot reload, then add longer dependency-graph integration evidence.

entries.name: Decision lifecycle and reset
entries.state: Reset ABI v1 is public at VM and facade layers and is restricted to idle decision boundaries. It preserves configuration, services, extensions, installed host functions/modules, lifetime peaks, and host-owned immutable CompiledModule values; discards all guest globals, heap objects, coroutines, programs, caches, diagnostics, coverage, and roots; restarts RNG, logical time, instruction counters, and deterministic GC scheduling; and epoch-invalidates every Function, Exports, and RetainedValue lease. A focused native mixed table/string/coroutine/program/retained-export workload holds exact VM-owned memory statistics after warmup through 600 decisions; a Node/V8 wasm32 probe covers the same lifecycle and exact plateau across 300 decisions.
entries.future_plan: Add external dedicated-Linux long-running-host evidence and keep the reset plus typed-invocation contracts stable.

entries.name: Serde bridge
entries.state: Owned-value serde paths exist, and OwnedTable can deserialize string-keyed fields plus array slots through serde.
entries.future_plan: Add binary and graph-preserving owned serde, then a lifetime-safe live/zero-copy path after the public value surface stabilizes.

entries.name: Retained handles
entries.state: Script function and export handles are true collector roots. They can be retained, called, inspected for their install generation and decision epoch, checked for freshness, and accessed through fail-closed current-generation/current-epoch call/value/get/function/deserialize paths. Repeated slot reuse cannot make stale handles alias replacement objects or programs; reset invalidates every clone while ordinary retained calls remain valid across hot reload outside reset epochs.
entries.future_plan: Keep generation and epoch failures explicit as richer live-value handles are introduced.

entries.name: Hot reload
entries.state: Compile/install/hot-reload entry points and source-named run helpers exist; tests cover source-name diagnostics, public runtime-location accessors, failed-reload old-program survival, generation-stamped true-root handles, epoch invalidation on decision reset, stale-handle fail-closed access, and reclamation/reuse of obsolete bytecode, constants, caches, and coverage after the final reachable reference drops. Runtime-failing reload can still leave partial global/heap effects because execution is not transactional.
entries.future_plan: Add transactional or isolated runtime-failure behavior, module dependencies, migration docs, and broader install-time diagnostics.

entries.name: Macro/codegen sugar
entries.state: Macro sugar exists as an early slice, but the lower-level API should lead.
entries.future_plan: Delay expansion until the core API stops moving.

entries.name: Harness CLI and schema
entries.state: bench/ has a standalone-style CLI, package metadata, machine-readable inventory, validated JSONL history schema, refreshable RESULTS.md, current-results JSON, generated per-workload claim gating, retained fixed-work A/B evidence, and a separate paired many-VM memory evidence schema.
entries.future_plan: Keep JSONL as the source of truth for CI and website data.

entries.name: Adapter matrix

entries.future_plan: Split adapters into standalone crates/binaries and keep baselines current.

entries.name: Workloads
entries.state: Five default workload families are wired, with 18 workload entries present; #15 string-building/concat has cross-adapter source coverage, #16–#18 provide portable burst/churn/intentional-retention probes, and #19–#21 provide deterministic steady/history/intentional-retention todo-app probes for Luau and Koto. A coherent 990-process cross-engine memory baseline and the 99-sample safe-memory Rustia refresh are committed.
entries.future_plan: Expand the remaining #12 interop, #13 serde, and #14 fuel/limit workload plan, then broaden mixed-heap pressure and intentional measurement history.

entries.name: History and static report
entries.state: A coherent Linux-only speed snapshot covers 12 adapter families plus verified mlua/Luau JIT. The generated dashboard includes ranked speed bars, workload heatmaps, performance history, three memory workload cohorts, and Rustia peak/retained history versus a fixed mlua/JIT reference. The current memory view preserves frozen competitor rows while refreshing Rustia from safe-memory-588b541.
entries.future_plan: Accumulate longer performance and memory history, then publish richer regression annotations after the standalone split.

entries.name: Benchmark operations
entries.state: Hosted CI validates committed artifacts without provisioning billed infrastructure. An operator can manually start a Rustia-only Linode memory cohort for an exact commit already present on main. The explicit bounded Linode lifecycle promotes only complete evidence after confirmed instance deletion. The cgroup-v2 memory supervisor/analyzer, current/history merge, dashboard, frozen 990-process cross-engine baseline, 99-sample safe-memory Rustia refresh, and wasm32 quota probe are implemented.
entries.future_plan: Keep the Linode lifecycle reproducible, accumulate coherent history, broaden mixed-heap pressure, and add regression alerts without mixing developer-machine timings.

entries.name: Wasm-emit JIT spike
entries.state: Runtime wasm emission is validated in spikes, not production-integrated.
entries.future_plan: Add type guards/deopt and interpreter-equivalence checks before production use.

entries.name: Native/wasm matrix
entries.state: A coherent 12-adapter-family native Linux baseline plus a verified mlua/Luau JIT mode is recorded; recurring wasm target results cover rustia+koto+rhai and br_table/call_ref dispatch on Node/V8, while the accepted four-runtime matrix remains archived as historical portability evidence.
entries.future_plan: Broaden public baselines and keep result history fresh across runtime updates.

entries.name: Workspace tests and release preflight
entries.state: Production crates have meaningful unit and conformance tests; just release-preflight composes release artifact checks, crate metadata checks, workflow policy checks, generated leaf package dry-run checks, explicit public-example compilation, and cargo test --workspace; hosted CI mirrors that gate.
entries.future_plan: Keep expanding tests with new runtime/API work and keep CI aligned with release-preflight.

entries.name: CLI
entries.state: rustia-cli supports file, stdin, --eval, and --repl execution with profile, fuel, and source-name options; state-preserving line evaluation and expression shorthand; source-aware compile/runtime diagnostics; and a fixed-order filesystem require adapter with canonical cache identities, nested referrer-relative resolution, and module-source runtime diagnostics. Deterministic CLI execution deliberately has no ambient filesystem resolver.
entries.future_plan: Add richer multiline editing/history behavior and stack-aware diagnostic formatting; keep filesystem resolution policy stable and covered across supported hosts.

entries.name: Live wasm demo
entries.state: demos/live-wasm can build and serve a browser demo outside normal workspace gates.
entries.future_plan: Refresh after production wasm/perf work and make it a public example.

entries.name: Crate publishability
entries.state: Workspace crates are still publish = false, but generated crate metadata audit, explicit internal dependency versions, publishability-derived leaf package dry-run checks in preflight/CI, package file-list audit, publishability blocker audit, release checklist, semver policy, changelog validation, and release preflight are present.
entries.future_plan: Flip policy only after P1 gates, then publish/remove internal dependency blockers in generated order.
